Protocol.Name: PathLinks_Clinical_Decision_Support
Protocol.Description: Blood Result Actioning Protocol for Primary Care
Protocol.Author: PathLinks Clinical Governance

Action.Title: ⚠️ CRITICAL: Hyperkalaemia Alert
Action.Text:
Potassium ≥ 6.0 mmol/L detected.
IMMEDIATE ACTIONS: 1. Obtain ECG immediately 2. If K ≥ 6.5 mmol/L → Urgent hospital admission 3. Review medications: ACEi, ARBs, Spironolactone, NSAIDs, Trimethoprim 4. Consider IV Calcium Gluconate if ECG changes present
CODING: Add Read Code 44I7. (Serum potassium raised)

Action.Title: ⚠️ CRITICAL: Severe Hyponatraemia
Action.Text:
Sodium < 125 mmol/L detected.
IMMEDIATE ACTIONS: 1. Assess for symptoms (confusion, seizure, nausea) 2. If symptomatic → Urgent hospital admission 3. Review medications (Diuretics, SSRIs, PPIs) 4. Check fluid status and osmolality
CODING: Add Read Code 44I5. (Serum sodium low)

Action.Title: ⚠️ CRITICAL: Severe Hypertriglyceridaemia
Action.Text:
Triglycerides > 10 mmol/L detected.
⚠️ HIGH RISK OF ACUTE PANCREATITIS
IMMEDIATE ACTIONS: 1. Urgent referral to Lipid/Metabolic Specialist 2. Consider admission if symptomatic (abdominal pain) 3. Stop alcohol completely 4. Start Fibrate therapy if tolerated
CODING: Add Read Code 44P.. (Serum lipids)

Action.Title: 🩸 Anaemia Detected (Male)
Action.Text:
Haemoglobin < 130 g/L in male patient.
CLINICAL PATHWAY: 1. Check MCV to classify anaemia type: - Microcytic (<80): Check Ferritin, consider GI bleed - Normocytic (80-100): Check reticulocytes, CKD, chronic disease - Macrocytic (>100): Check B12, Folate, TFTs, alcohol history
2. If age >60 or red flags (weight loss, change in bowel habit): → Perform FIT test → Consider 2WW referral if FIT positive
3. Check Ferritin, B12, Folate, Reticulocytes
EMIS CODING: 422.. (Anaemia screen done)

Action.Title: 🩸 Anaemia Detected (Female)
Action.Text:
Haemoglobin < 115 g/L in female patient.
CLINICAL PATHWAY: 1. Check MCV to classify anaemia type 2. Consider menstrual history (menorrhagia?) 3. If post-menopausal or age >60: FIT test / 2WW consideration 4. Check Ferritin, B12, Folate
EMIS CODING: 422.. (Anaemia screen done)

Action.Title: 🔬 Iron Deficiency Confirmed
Action.Text:
Ferritin < 30 µg/L confirms iron deficiency.
CLINICAL PATHWAY: 1. Identify cause of iron loss: - Menorrhagia (pre-menopausal women) - GI blood loss (post-menopausal / males → 2WW consideration) - Coeliac disease (check tTG antibodies)
2. Treatment: - Start oral iron (Ferrous Fumarate 210mg TDS) - Recheck Hb/Ferritin in 4 weeks
⚠️ RED FLAG: Low ferritin in males or post-menopausal females WITHOUT clear cause requires GI investigation.
EMIS CODING: D00y. (Iron deficiency anaemia)

Action.Title: 📊 Prediabetes / High Risk Detected
Action.Text:
HbA1c 42-47 mmol/mol = PREDIABETES
CLINICAL PATHWAY: 1. Refer to National Diabetes Prevention Programme (NDPP) 2. Lifestyle advice: Diet, Exercise, Weight management 3. Re-test HbA1c annually 4. QRISK3 assessment if not done recently
EMIS CODING: C109. (Diabetes mellitus at risk)

Action.Title: 🩺 Type 2 Diabetes: New Diagnosis Range
Action.Text:
HbA1c 48-57 mmol/mol = TYPE 2 DIABETES THRESHOLD
CLINICAL PATHWAY (NG28): 1. Confirm diagnosis (repeat HbA1c if asymptomatic) 2. Lifestyle advice (STRUCTURED education offer) 3. Offer Metformin 500mg OD (titrate slowly) 4. Target HbA1c: 48 mmol/mol (or 53 if dual therapy)
EARLY SGLT2 TRIGGER: → If CVD risk >10%, Heart Failure, or CKD Stage 3+: Consider early SGLT2i (e.g., Dapagliflozin)
EMIS CODING: C10F. (Type 2 diabetes mellitus)

Action.Title: ⚠️ Diabetes: Poor Control
Action.Text:
HbA1c ≥ 75 mmol/mol = POOR GLYCAEMIC CONTROL
CLINICAL PATHWAY: 1. Review medication adherence 2. Consider triple therapy or GLP-1 RA if BMI >35 3. If symptomatic (Polyuria/Polydipsia): Consider Insulin initiation 4. Discuss with Diabetes Specialist Nurse or refer
⚠️ Check for diabetic complications: - Retinopathy screening up to date? - Foot check completed? - Renal function (eGFR) and uACR checked?
EMIS CODING: 66Ao. (Diabetic on maximal treatment)

Action.Title: 💊 Cholesterol Elevated - QRISK Assessment
Action.Text:
Total Cholesterol > 5.0 mmol/L
CLINICAL PATHWAY: 1. Calculate QRISK3 score (if not done in last 12 months) 2. If QRISK3 ≥ 10%: → Offer Atorvastatin 20mg → Lifestyle advice 3. If QRISK3 < 10%: → Lifestyle advice only → Recheck in 5 years (or annually if borderline)
NON-HDL TARGET: - Primary prevention: < 4.0 mmol/L - Secondary prevention (existing CVD): < 2.5 mmol/L
EMIS CODING: 38DR. (QRISK2 CVD 10-year risk)

Action.Title: 🔬 ALT Elevated
Action.Text:
ALT > 40 IU/L (above upper limit)
CLINICAL PATHWAY: 1. MASLD Screen: Check BMI, HbA1c, Lipids 2. Alcohol history (calculate units/week) 3. If ALT > 3x ULN (>120 IU/L): → Viral Hepatitis Screen (HBsAg, HCV Ab) → Consider autoimmune liver screen (ANA, SMA) 4. Review medications (Statins, Paracetamol, Methotrexate)
FIB-4 SCORE: Age, AST, ALT, Platelets → Risk-stratify fibrosis
EMIS CODING: 662.. (Liver function test abnormal)

Action.Title: 🦋 Overt Hypothyroidism
Action.Text:
TSH > 10.0 mU/L (with likely low Free T4)
CLINICAL PATHWAY: 1. Confirm diagnosis (check Free T4) 2. Start Levothyroxine: - Age <65, no cardiac history: Start 50-100mcg OD - Age >65 or cardiac history: Start 25mcg OD 3. Recheck TFTs in 6-8 weeks 4. Target TSH: 0.4 - 2.0 mU/L
EMIS CODING: C10.. (Hypothyroidism)

Action.Title: 🔬 PSA Elevated
Action.Text:
PSA > 4.0 ng/mL detected
⚠️ BEFORE 2WW REFERRAL, EXCLUDE: 1. Recent UTI (treat and wait 1 month) 2. Recent ejaculation (wait 48 hours) 3. Vigorous exercise / cycling 4. Recent DRE (wait 1 week)
AGE-SPECIFIC THRESHOLDS: - 40-49: > 2.5 ng/mL abnormal - 50-59: > 3.5 ng/mL abnormal - 60-69: > 4.5 ng/mL abnormal - 70-79: > 6.5 ng/mL abnormal
If confirmed elevated after exclusions → 2WW Urology Referral
EMIS CODING: 4K15. (Serum PSA level raised)

Action.Title: 🩺 CA125 Elevated
Action.Text:
CA125 ≥ 35 U/mL
NICE CG122 PATHWAY: 1. Urgent Pelvic Ultrasound (within 2 weeks) 2. If US abnormal → 2WW Gynaecology referral 3. Consider other causes: Endometriosis, Fibroids, Ovarian cysts
RMI (Risk of Malignancy Index) calculation required.
EMIS CODING: 44M5. (Serum CA125 level raised)

Action.Title: 🩺 eGFR < 60 - Possible CKD
Action.Text:
eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73m² detected
CLINICAL PATHWAY: 1. Repeat in 2 weeks to confirm (rule out AKI) 2. If persistent: - Check uACR (albuminuria) - Review medications (NSAIDs, ACEi dose) - BP target < 140/90 (or < 130/80 if proteinuria)
CKD STAGING: - Stage 3a: eGFR 45-59 - Stage 3b: eGFR 30-44 - Stage 4: eGFR 15-29 (Nephrology referral) - Stage 5: eGFR <15 (Urgent nephrology)
EMIS CODING: 1Z1.. (Chronic kidney disease stage 3)

Action.Title: ⚠️ HIV Screening Reactive
Action.Text:
HIV screening test REACTIVE
IMMEDIATE ACTIONS: 1. Urgent referral to GUM/Infectious Disease Specialist 2. Confirmatory Western Blot test required 3. If antenatal: Urgent HIV specialist/antenatal team involvement 4. PREVENT vertical transmission
Do NOT disclose to patient until confirmatory test complete.
EMIS CODING: 65V.. (HIV positive)

Action.Title: ⚠️ Hepatitis B Positive
Action.Text:
Hepatitis B Surface Antigen (HBsAg) POSITIVE
Indicates ACTIVE HBV infection.
ACTIONS: 1. Check: HBeAg, Anti-HBe, HBV DNA Viral Load 2. Refer to Hepatology/GI for assessment 3. Screen household contacts
IF PREGNANT: → Urgent referral to specialist antenatal team → Infant requires HBIG + Vaccination at birth
EMIS CODING: A707. (Hepatitis B carrier)
